text:
sophia: follow-up from the RFC thread 1: we need a clear, small set of runtime defaults for SDKs (python/ts/go) so users don't get bitten by subtle transport/retry/pagination differences

dave: agree. goal: safe, obvious defaults for 90% of users, plus opt-ins for advanced behavior. what do folks think about per-language defaults?

maria: proposal: JS/TS -> HTTP/2 streaming (fetch + ReadableStream) by default in node/browser, fall back to unary HTTP if streaming not available. Go -> gRPC by default. Python -> HTTP (httpx requests) by default, grpc optional via extras.

eli: reasoning: python ecosystems prefer small deps; grpc forces a lot of surface area. we can ship an opt-in "grpc" extra for py users that need perf.

harrison: good. we should make the transport pluggable in the Client constructor but default to "auto" semantics that pick the recommendation per runtime. e.g., Client(transport=\"auto\") vs Client(transport=\"grpc\").

sophia: retries: default only for idempotent calls (GET-like). default attempts=3, base_backoff=200ms, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full. also cap total retry window at 10s for interactive calls.

dave: important: surface an opt-out & per-call override API. Users need to declare "non_idempotent=true" to prevent accidental retries. also expose a RetryPolicy object for advanced configs.

maria: pagination: server returns opaque resume_token + optional page_info. prefer token-based pagination (opaque cursor) over offsets. token format suggestion: server emits `resume_token=\"v1:base64(payload)\"` and an expiry header/field `resume_expires_at` (RFC3339).

eli: why include version prefix? Allows us to rotate server-side encoding without breaking clients. clients should treat token as opaque string.

harrison: on client ergonomics: iterate yields items not pages. py: provide sync generator `for item in client.list_things(...):` and async generator `async for item in client.list_things_async(...):`. ts/node: async iterable `for await (const item of client.listThings())`. go: `it := client.ListThings(ctx, req); for it.Next() { item := it.Item() }` with `it.Err()` and `it.Close()` semantics.

sophia: paging defaults: page_size default=100, server_enforced max_page_size=1000. clients can request up to the server cap. also SDKs should expose `max_page_size` in the client config to avoid accidental huge pages.

dave: resume semantics for streaming chat: server will emit a `resume_token` in stream metadata at stable checkpoints. clients can persist it. small helper in SDK: `client.save_resume_token(token)` and `client.resume_from(token)`. include example in docs.

maria: example response sketch (HTTP JSON): ```json
{
  "items": [ ... ],
  "resume_token": "v1:YXJyaXZlZA==",
  "page_info": {"has_more": true}
}
```

harrison: retries + pagination gotcha: only retry page fetches that are idempotent. if a page request is documented as "consumes from server cursor" (consumption cursor), mark it non-idempotent. default assumption: list endpoints are idempotent unless explicitly documented otherwise. we should mark any consuming endpoints in the API spec.

els: backpressure: for streaming transports (http2/grpc) default client buffer_size=64 items. behavior when buffer full: apply built-in backpressure (pause reading from network) where supported, otherwise emit a warning + drop-oldest metric and continue. document tradeoffs.

sophia: telemetry: record transport_chosen, retries_attempted, retry_duration_ms, pagination_mode (offset|token), page_size_requested, final_status. these will help tune defaults.

dave: surface transport selection in logs/metrics so we can see real-world usage. also add a warning in SDK if user forces grpc on python without installing extras.

maria: upgrade/migration policy: changing token format is a major semver bump. we should include a migration header in server responses when we plan to change encoding: `X-Resume-Next-Version: v2` and a transition timeline.

eli: small ergonomic APIs to add: python `PagedIterator.peek_buffered()`, ts `client.listThings({pageSize}).byPage()` for page-level control, go `Pager.NextPage(ctx)` for advanced use. but keep the default item-level iteration simple.

harrison: docs checklist: per-language default table, code snippets for persisting resume tokens, explicit note about idempotency and retries, backpressure section for streaming, telemetry fields. I'll add Go examples for Next/Close.

sophia: agree. action items: 1) doc table + default table per language (dave), 2) python snippet + opt-in grpc extras (maria), 3) ts/streaming backpressure example (eli), 4) go iterator + telemetry hooks (harrison). I'll update the RFC draft with all of this and call out the migration policy.

dave: one more question: should we expose a global default_retry_policy in the top-level client config? i think yes, with sane defaults and per-call override.

maria: yes. `Client(defaults=ClientDefaults(retry_policy=..., page_size=...))` feels right. keep top-level args flat for ergonomics.

els: +1.

harrison: +1.

sophia: consensus seems clear. final check: idempotent-only retries by default?

everyone: +1 :thumbsup:
